label: A record is JSON
gloss: every record a flow carries is a set of named fields - and underneath, every tool stores it as JSON
why: Whatever the tool calls it - dynamic content in Power Automate, a bundle in Make, an item in n8n, the data-out fields in Zapier, a dict in Python - the record a step receives is a JSON object: field names in quotes, values after colons. When a step misbehaves, reading that object as the step sees it is how you find out why. Here the PO lookup finds nothing for INV-1; the record will tell you why.
cue: when a lookup or expression comes back empty, open the record and read the field names it actually has
task: The PO lookup matches on poNumber but comes back empty for INV-1. Read the record as it arrived, find the field the lookup needs, and fix the record so PO-1 is found and variance computes.
notes: Keys are always in double quotes: "poNumber", not poNumber.
Numbers are bare: 1220, not "1220" and not "$1,220.00".
Text is in double quotes; true, false and null are bare words.
Commas between fields, none after the last one; braces { } wrap an object, brackets [ ] wrap a list.

checks.label: INV-1 carries its PO (poTotal 1200)

dialect.powerAutomate: dynamic content / 'Parse JSON' - the trigger output body is this object
dialect.powerAppsCopilot: a record in Power Fx ({ poNumber: "PO-1", ... }) or a Dataverse row
dialect.make: a bundle - the output panel of each module shows the fields
dialect.n8n: an item ({ "json": { ... } }) - the output panel shows it as table or JSON
dialect.zapier: the 'Data out' fields shown when you test a step
dialect.langgraph: the state object (a TypedDict) passed from node to node
